question_text: A 76-year-old man is brought to the emergency room because of one episode of hemoptysis. His pulse is 110/min. Physical examination shows pallor; there is blood in the oral cavity. Examination of the nasal cavity with a nasal speculum shows active bleeding from the posterior nasal cavity. Tamponade with a balloon catheter is attempted without success. The most appropriate next step in the management is ligation of a branch of a vessel of which of the following arteries?

                    ### Question
                    A 76-year-old man is brought to the emergency room because of one episode of hemoptysis. His pulse is 110/min. Physical examination shows pallor; there is blood in the oral cavity. Examination of the nasal cavity with a nasal speculum shows active bleeding from the posterior nasal cavity. Tamponade with a balloon catheter is attempted without success. The most appropriate next step in the management is ligation of a branch of a vessel of which of the following arteries?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Ophthalmic artery
opb. Anterior cerebral artery
opc. Facial artery
opd. Occipital artery
ope. Maxillary artery

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the management of active bleeding from the posterior nasal cavity, if tamponade with a balloon catheter is unsuccessful, the most appropriate next step would be ligation of a branch of the maxillary artery.
